exercises.heading: 3.8. Exercises

problem.paragraph: A population of the yeast cell Saccharomyces cerevisiae (a yeast used for fermentation) develops with a constant relative growth rate of $$0.4159$$ per hour. The initial population consists of $$3.8$$ million cells. Find the population size after $$2$$ hours.

A common inhabitant of human intestines is the bacterium Escherichia coli, named after the German pediatrician Theodor Escherich, who identified it in 1885. A cell of this bacterium in a nutrient-broth medium divides into two cells every $$20$$ minutes. The initial population of a culture is $$50$$ cells.

list.item: Find the relative growth rate.
Find an expression for the number of cells after $$t$$ hours.
Find the number of cells after $$6$$ hours.
Find the rate of growth after $$6$$ hours.
When will the population reach a million cells?

problem.paragraph: A culture of the bacterium Salmonella enteritidis initially contains $$50$$ cells. When introduced into a nutrient broth, the culture grows at a rate proportional to its size. After $$1.5$$ hours the population has increased to $$975$$ .

list.item: Find an expression for the number of bacteria after $$t$$ hours.
Find the number of bacteria after $$3$$ hours.
Find the rate of growth after $$3$$ hours.
After how many hours will the population reach $$250,000$$ ?

problem.paragraph: A bacteria culture grows with constant relative growth rate. The bacteria count was $$400$$ after $$2$$ hours and $$25,600$$ after $$6$$ hours.

list.item: What is the relative growth rate? Express your answer as a percentage.
What was the initial size of the culture?
Find an expression for the number of bacteria after $$t$$ hours.
Find the number of bacteria after $$4.5$$ hours.
Find the rate of growth after $$4.5$$ hours.
When will the population reach $$50,000$$ ?

problem.paragraph: The table gives estimates of the world population, in millions, from 1750 to 2000.

list.item: Use the exponential model and the population figures for 1750 and 1800 to predict the world population in 1900 and 1950. Compare with the actual figures.
Use the exponential model and the population figures for 1850 and 1900 to predict the world population in 1950. Compare with the actual population.
Use the exponential model and the population figures for 1900 and 1950 to predict the world population in 2000. Compare with the actual population and try to explain the discrepancy.

solution.paragraph: $$3972$$ million; wars in the first half of century, increased life expectancy in second half

problem.paragraph: The table gives census data for the population of Indonesia, in millions, during the second half of the $$20$$ th century.

list.item: Assuming the population grows at a rate proportional to its size, use the census data for 1950 and 1960 to predict the population in 1980. Compare with the actual figure.
Use the census data for 1960 and 1980 to predict the population in 2000. Compare with the actual population.
Use the census data for 1980 and 2000 to predict the population in 2010 and compare with the actual population of $$243$$ million.
Use the model in part (c) to predict the population in 2025. Do you think the prediction will be too high or too low? Why?

problem.paragraph: Experiments show that if the chemical reaction
$$\left. N_{2}O_{5}\rightarrow 2{NO}_{2} + \frac{1}{2}O_{2} \right.$$
takes place at $$45{}_{}^{}$$ , the rate of reaction of dinitrogen pentoxide is proportional to its concentration as follows:
$$- \frac{d\left\lbrack {N_{2}O_{5}} \right\rbrack}{\mathit{dt}} = 0.0005\left\lbrack {N_{2}O_{5}} \right\rbrack$$

list.item: Find an expression for the concentration $$\left\lbrack {N_{2}O_{5}} \right\rbrack$$ after $$t$$ seconds if the initial concentration is $$C$$ .
How long will the reaction take to reduce the concentration of $$N_{2}O_{5}$$ to $$90\%$$ of its original value?

problem.paragraph: Chromium- $$51$$ has a half-life of $$28$$ days.

list.item: A sample has initial mass $$50$$ mg initially. Find a formula for the mass remaining after $$t$$ days.
Find the mass remaining after $$40$$ days.
How long does it take the sample to decay to a mass of $$2$$ mg?
Sketch the graph of the mass function.

problem.paragraph: The half-life of cesium- $$137$$ is $$30$$ years. Suppose we have a $$100$$ -mg sample.

list.item: Find the mass that remains after $$t$$ years.
How much of the sample remains after $$100$$ years?
After how long will only $$1$$ mg remain?

problem.paragraph: A sample of einsteinium- $$252$$ decayed to $$64.3\%$$ of its original mass after $$300$$ days.

list.item: What is the half-life of einsteinium- $$252$$ ?
How long would it take the sample to decay to one-third of its original mass?

exercises.paragraph: 11, 12 and 13 Radiocarbon Dating Scientists can determine the age of ancient objects by the method of radiocarbon dating. The bombardment of the upper atmosphere by cosmic rays converts nitrogen to a radioactive isotope of carbon, $${}_{}^{}{}$$ , with a half-life of about $$5730$$ years. Vegetation absorbs carbon dioxide through the atmosphere and animal life assimilates $${}_{}^{}{}$$ through food chains. When a plant or animal dies, it stops replacing its carbon and the amount of $${}_{}^{}{}$$ present begins to decrease through radioactive decay. Therefore the level of radioactivity must also decay exponentially.

problem.paragraph: A discovery revealed a parchment fragment that had about $$74\%$$ as much $${}_{}^{}{}$$ radioactivity as does plant material on the earth today. Estimate the age of the parchment.

Dinosaur fossils are too old to be reliably dated using carbon-14. Suppose we had a 68-million-year-old dinosaur fossil. What fraction of the living dinosaur’s $${}_{}^{}{}$$ would be remaining today? Suppose the minimum detectable mass is $$0.1\%$$ . What is the maximum age of a fossil that could be dated using $${}_{}^{}{}$$ ?

Dinosaur fossils are often dated by using an element other than carbon, such as potassium-40, that has a longer half-life (in this case, approximately $$1.25$$ billion years). Suppose the minimum detectable mass is $$0.1\%$$ and a dinosaur is dated with $${}_{}^{}{}$$ to be 68 million years old. Is such a dating possible? In other words, what is the maximum age of a fossil that we could be dated using $${}_{}^{}{}$$ ?

A curve passes through the point $$\left( {0,5} \right)$$ and has the property that the slope of the curve at every point $$P$$ is twice the $$y$$ -coordinate of $$P$$ . What is the equation of the curve?
A roast turkey is removed from an oven when its temperature has reached $$185{}_{}^{}$$ and is placed on a table in a room where the ambient temperature is $$75{}_{}^{}$$ .

list.item: If the temperature of the turkey is $$150{}_{}^{}$$ after half an hour, what is the temperature after $$45$$ minutes?
When will the turkey have cooled to $$100{}_{}^{}$$ ?

problem.paragraph: In a murder investigation, the temperature of the corpse was $$32.5{}_{}^{}$$ at 1:30 PM and $$30.3{}_{}^{}$$ an hour later. Normal body temperature is $$37.0{}_{}^{}$$ and the ambient temperature was $$20.0{}_{}^{}$$ . When did the murder take place?
When a cold drink is taken from a refrigerator, its temperature is $$5{}_{}^{}$$ . After $$25$$ minutes in a $$20{}_{}^{}$$ room its temperature has increased to $$10{}_{}^{}$$ .

list.item: What is the temperature of the drink after $$50$$ minutes?
When will its temperature reach $$15{}_{}^{}$$ ?

problem.paragraph: A freshly brewed cup of coffee has temperature $$95{}_{}^{}$$ in a $$20{}_{}^{}$$ room. When its temperature is $$70{}_{}^{}$$ , it is cooling at a rate of $$1{}_{}^{}$$ per minute. When does this occur?

The rate of change of atmospheric pressure $$P$$ with respect to altitude $$h$$ is proportional to $$P$$ , provided that the temperature is constant. At $$15{}_{}^{}$$ the pressure is $$101.3$$ kPa at sea level and $$87.14$$ kPa at $$h = 1000$$ m.

list.item: What is the pressure at an altitude of $$3000$$ m?
What is the pressure at the top of Mount McKinley, at an altitude of $$6187$$ m?
If $$\$ 2500$$ is borrowed at $$4.5\%$$ interest, find the amounts due at the end of $$3$$ years if the interest is compounded annually, quarterly, monthly, weekly, daily, hourly, and continuously.

Suppose $$\$ 2500$$ is borrowed and the interest is compounded continuously. If $$A(t)$$ is the amount due after $$t$$ years, where $$0 \leqslant t \leqslant 3$$ , graph $$A(t)$$ for each of the interest rates $$5\%$$ , $$6\%$$ , and $$7\%$$ on a common screen.

If $$\$ 4000$$ is invested at $$1.75\%$$ interest, find the value of the investment at the end of $$5$$ years if the interest is compounded annually, semiannually, monthly, weekly, daily, and continuously.
If $$A(t)$$ is the amount of the investment at time $$t$$ for the case of continuous compounding, write a differential equation and an initial condition satisfied by $$A(t)$$ .
How long will it take an investment to double in value if the interest rate is $$3\%$$ compounded continuously?
What is the equivalent annual interest rate?
